You will work across the Portfolio focusing on the technical thread of customer missions—from requirements capture through system acceptance and delivery—acting as the technical authority/interface between the customer and ICEYE's engineering, product, and operations teams. Your role bridges program governance and system engineering: ensuring mission requirements are understood, flowed down, tracked, and validated, while maintaining configuration control and driving cross-functional technical alignment throughout the program lifecycle. This role directly contributes to ICEYE's ambition to become the leading provider of space-based ISR infrastructure by scaling reliable, high-impact mission delivery globally. The role will be based in Athens at the ICEYE facility. Travel to customer sites is required. Who We Are ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth. ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system. ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future. Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. ROLE HIGHLIGHTS - Quality Assurance Technician - Assembly, Integration & Final Inspection - Location: Valencia, Spain - Department: Product & Mission Assurance - Reports to: Reliability Engineer Manager - Employment type: Permanent - Workplace model: Production floor/Cleanroom - Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required) WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS: As a Quality Assurance Technician you are the independent set of eyes between our production line and orbit. You will perform in-process and final inspections of electronic and mechanical assemblies, verify that every integration step is carried out to procedure, and carry out the final inspection of completed satellites before they leave for environmental testing and launch. You will witness mandatory inspection points (MIPs), confirm workmanship against IPC and ECSS requirements, check torque, bonding, harness routing, connector mating and cleanliness, and make sure the build record is complete and audit-ready. Embedded within the production and AIT (Assembly, Integration and Test) environment, you will work in cleanrooms with ESD-sensitive flight hardware. Working closely with Production, AIT Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Mission Assurance and Supply Chain, you will catch defects before they move downstream, prevent quality escapes, and help every satellite we ship meet space-grade standards. You will lead four supply chain categories: Mechanical Systems and Manufacturing Enablement; Flight Control, Power and Structure; Electronics and Communication; and Optical and Inter Satellite Link. The supply chain teams of our sister companies in Spain, Poland, Germany and Greece will also report to you. You will be accountable for a large, strategically critical annual procurement spend, and for turning category strategies into continuous supply for serial production. You will work closely with the Director, Supply Chain Strategy, who supports your categories with risk assessment, supplier development and partnerships. This role is for a hands-on, technically grounded leader with a strong mechanical and electromechanical background, who has managed complex, highly regulated supply chains across countries and cultures.
